title: Pineapple express a flood threat to California, Southwest

 Advertisement Pineapple Express could bring Halloween weekend flooding to Southwest
 After flooding last week, an unusually moist weather system will soak the Desert Southwest. Here's the latest forecast.
 By Jonathan Erdman • 4 hours ago Updated: October 30, 2026, 9:24 am EDT Published: October 30, 2026, 9:00 am EDT Share Share
 1 . When and where will these soakings arrive? Chevron Down 
 An atmospheric river referred to as the "pineapple express" could bring heavy rain to parts of the Desert Southwest and Southern California over Halloween weekend, just over a week after destructive flooding plagued parts of Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico and Utah.
 This latest round of rain will be fueled by a low-end pineapple express , a type of atmospheric river that often fuels heavy rain events in the West, especially in a stronger El Niño winter. 
 ( COMPLETE COVERAGE: Super El Niño of 2026-27 )

 When and where will these soakings arrive?
 There are two rounds of soaking rain:
 Friday : Western Texas, parts of New Mexico and Arizona
 This weekend : In mainly Southern California, it will increase starting Saturday, peaking early Sunday. In the Southwest, rain and some high mountain snow will increase late Saturday, continue into Sunday and linger in some areas Monday.
 What are the potential impacts?
 Local flash flooding is possible from the first round of rain in parts of western Texas including Lubbock and Midland.

 A more serious flash flood threat is in play for the Desert Southwest. 
 That's because the ground is still saturated from the 2 to 5 inches of rain that soaked the area last week, triggering major flash flooding in northern Arizona , New Mexico, southern Colorado and southern Utah . 
 It's also because some of these areas will see both rounds of rain in a span of just three days.
 The map below shows total rainfall from both systems in the Southwest. Areas shaded in darker green and yellow could see more dangerous, widespread flash flooding. 
 The areas of greatest concern are:
 The Phoenix metro's north and east sides and the Mogollon Rim of northern Arizona
 The canyonlands of southern Utah
 Elevations below snow level in western Colorado
 Any ground scorched by recent wildfires, which is particularly susceptible to producing fast-moving debris flows, rock and mudslides, even in modest rainfall. 
 According to the National Weather Service in Flagstaff, Arizona, rivers such as the Little Colorado and Verde, could run high for days after this weekend's latest soaking.
 If you had weekend plans to do any hiking in the parks of southern Utah, southern Colorado and Arizona, you should consider canceling. Fast-moving, life-threatening flash floods can sweep rapidly through slot canyons. 
 Over the higher elevations, this precipitation may fall as snow over the higher peaks of the Rockies and Sierra. This may lead to slippery travel mainly Sunday into Monday over mountain passes. 
 Record moisture for Halloween weekend?
 What's fueling this soaking is a southward plunge of the jet stream off the West Coast. 
 That jet stream will pull a ribbon of deep tropical moisture called an atmospheric river into the Southwest. 
 This particular atmospheric river tap is originating from near Hawaii, something meteorologists nickname the "pineapple express."
 This is the forecast weather pattern for Halloween weekend, showing an atmospheric river headed into California and the Southwest.
 It's not a strong version of either an atmospheric river or pineapple express, but the moisture fueling this heavy rain could be record-setting for this time of year.
 According to the National Weather Service, the total moisture in the atmosphere over parts of Arizona, Colorado, Nevada and Utah could be 2 to 3 times the average for the end of October, near record amounts for Halloween weekend. 
 This could be a harbinger, given the tendency for a wetter Southwest during most stronger El Niños from fall through spring.
